title: Build an in-memory task scheduler in Go with status transitions and filtering
description: Multi-step Go task: implement a task store with CRUD, then add status transitions (pending→running→done/failed), then add priority-based listing. All tests are injected.

task_spec.prompt:
Create internal/scheduler/scheduler.go implementing a task scheduler in three steps.

Step 1 — Basic CRUD:
  type Status string constants: StatusPending, StatusRunning, StatusDone, StatusFailed
  type Task struct { ID int; Name string; Priority int; Status Status }
  func New() *Scheduler
  func (s *Scheduler) Create(name string, priority int) int  // returns new task ID
  func (s *Scheduler) Get(id int) (Task, bool)
  func (s *Scheduler) Len() int

Step 2 — Status transitions:
  func (s *Scheduler) Start(id int) error    // pending → running; error if wrong state
  func (s *Scheduler) Complete(id int) error // running → done; error if wrong state
  func (s *Scheduler) Fail(id int) error     // running → failed; error if wrong state

Step 3 — Priority listing:
  func (s *Scheduler) ListByPriority() []Task   // all tasks, highest priority first
  func (s *Scheduler) FilterByStatus(s Status) []Task

All 10 tests must pass.
Run: go test ./...
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
